To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a human small cell carcinoma of the lung, implanted in nude mice, spontaneously transformed the mouse cells by a mechanism of transfer of human tumor cell DNA to mouse cells in vivo, which was confirmed by transfection in vitro.

a human small cell carcinoma transplanted to nude mice can spontaneously induce malignancy in mouse fibroblast-like cells in vivo, and that this transformation of the mouse fibroblastlike cells in vivo is due to the presence of human tumor DNA.

a human small cell carcinoma of the lung implanted in nude mice can spontaneously transfer its DNA to mouse cells in vivo to produce a mouse tumor that is morphologically similar to the original human tumor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of tumor progression.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the induction and propagation of malignancy in vivo.
the study of the molecular basis of human cancer, with particular emphasis on the molecular mechanisms of human lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the human tumor xenografts in the nude mice were capable of transforming mouse cells in vivo and that the human tumor cells were capable of transferring genetic information to the transformed mouse cells.
the spontaneous induction of malignance in mouse cells by the implanted human tumor DNA is a novel and important finding.
human tumor DNA can be transferred to normal mouse cells by a xenografted human tumor and that the transferred tumor DNA may be the cause of transformation of the mouse cell to a malignant state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that human tumor cells can induce malignant transformation of mouse cells in vivo, and that the human tumor cells can do this spontaneously.
human tumor cells can transfer DNA to normal mouse cells in vivo, and this DNA can transform the mouse cells.
the spontaneous transformation of normal cells by human cancer cells in vivo can occur.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the transfer of human tumor cell DNA to mouse cells in vivo can result in the transformation of the latter cells to become malignant, and that the human tumor cell DNA is the cause of this malignant transformation of the mouse cell.
the human tumor cells can transfer genetic information to the mouse cells in the nude mice.
the transfer of DNA from a human tumor to mouse cells in vivo can induce malignancy in the mouse cells, suggesting that the DNA of human tumors can induce transformation in vivo.
